newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BASKET DEALS HIGHLIGHT BCE,FIRST DEAL FOR CZK MADE.
newsitem.headline: BASKET DEALS HIGHLIGHT BCE,FIRST DEAL FOR CZK MADE.

text.p: Basket deals for the U.S. dollar and the German mark highlighted average trading on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday, driving the most active December down for the mark and up for the dollar.
The first symbolic deal was concluded for the Czech crown, -- the eighth currency futures product of the BCE, launched one week ago -- at 5.30 forints, traders said.
"This deal was symbolic, little conclusion could be drawn from it," said Mihaly Eotvos of OTP Forex.
On the BCE, more than half of the day's total forex futures turnover of 24,388 lots or 4.072 billion forints were made for mark, while dollar and sterling deals also contributed substantially.
The most actively traded December mark gave up 15 fillers to settle at 116.81 forints, while December dollar put on 30 fillers to 196.40.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange's currency futures market, mark and dollar deals for August contributed 222.2 million forints and 94.1 million forints, respectively, to the turnover.
Both remained steady, the mark at 111.09 forints and the dollar at 186.23 forints.
The Hungarian forint floats within the central bank's 4.5 percent wide intervention range, against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
